page.layout: One printed page of verse, centred in the left two-thirds, with a signature line "I. Iacomotus Barrensis." below it and a woodcut ornament below that. Right side shows show-through and the edge of the neighbouring page, which are not transcribed. No running head, no page number, no catchword.

main_text.p:
V ana esse cuncta diserunt:
Nec quicquam in mundo certum mortalibus vllis
Durare quod queat diu.

Damnant vesanae gentis deliria, mortem
Vetant sibi conscisc ere.

Et tam multiplicis quae sit verissima causa
Quum vanitatis indicant,

Protinus exponunt istam quae fortia sanant
Contagionem Balsama.

Et quae solo leuet diros panacaea labores,
Curasque tristes perdomat.

Sit mens nostra Dei, dicunt, imbuta timore,
Huic vota pura nuncupet.

Hunc solum inssis veneretur cultibus, atque
Rebus molestis invocet.

Semper & Æthereae Legis praescripta sequatur
Per damna quaeuis & cruces.

Vilem spernat humum, quaerat caelestia opesque
Summo repostas aethere.

Hac Regis Sohymae est sententia certa fideles
Quae vanitate liberat.
main_text.head: I. Iacomotus Barrensis.

page.notes: The verse is printed in italic type; the lines are set with indents and are transcribed as paragraphs of stanza-like couplets. The right-hand edge shows show-through and the neighbouring page's text ("NSIS.") and is omitted. The woodcut ornament below the signature is not text. Some words in the scan are slightly blurred ("conscisc ere", "Sohymae", "inssis") and may be doubtful.
